summary:
w211 plan written (plan.md, parts 1-5), all 15 accepted requirements (26 scenarios) planned; Retires are the @r1/@r3 @deprecated titles.
The work-item's Answers settle 2-plan's questions: carrier is git on the upstream's remote (D10-D12): the asker pushes requests, answers and turns to its asker id's namespace, reads the upstream's published requests by fetch; settings and allow list in .shop/requests.toml; upstream publishes each changed request from another asker.
Supervision's raise unchanged (D9): the r30-r32 gate and the carrier run only in the work request command.
Take-in is `work take-in` (D7): fetches at start, allow-list check with a told reason (r41), writes through request/reply/turn's own checks; work run calls it before intake rounds (D13).
Sides from the repository's relation to the request (D2); repo id from spec/index.md for r32 (D3); gate order (D4); work show <request> (D5).
Live single-repository scenarios and work-queue r7 stay green as internal requests of a ctx-a repository (D6), which dissolves the r7 conflict; zero-line lines file left as is (D8).
File set: researcher's minus workqueue.py and supervise_raise.py, plus workqueue_sent.py, workqueue_takein.py, requests_send_steps.py, CLAUDE.md.
Open cases: newline in fields, several upstreams or internal requests in an asker repo, id collisions at take-in, take-in exit when items are left, push/fetch failures.
